standard_prerequisites.name: The Taylor expansion of a polynomial in two variables, f(x+y) = f(x) + f'(x)y + g(x,y)y^2
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at its first sentence
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identity that converts f(b) - f(a) into f'(a)(b-a) plus a multiple of (b-a)^2.

standard_prerequisites.name: In a local ring an element of the form 1 + m with m in the maximal ideal is a unit
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof in its last two sentences
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the factor 1 + f'(a)^{-1}c(b-a) into a unit so that the product vanishes only if b - a does.

core_obligations: Write the Taylor identity: express f(x + y) - f(x) as f'(x)y + g(x,y)y^2 in R[x,y], which the author states is immediate from expanding f(x+y) and leaves to the reader (proof lines 42318-42320).
Apply it to the two roots: from f(b) - f(a) = 0 obtain f'(a)(b-a) + c(b-a)^2 = 0 for some c in R (proof lines 42320-42322).
Use the two hypotheses: f'(a) is a unit, so the equation becomes (b-a)(1 + f'(a)^{-1}c(b-a)) = 0, and b - a lies in the maximal ideal, so the second factor is a unit (proof lines 42322-42325).
Conclude b - a = 0, which is the assertion (proof line 42325).
proof_roadmap: Expand f at a to turn the equality of values into a divisibility statement for b - a (proof lines 42318-42322).
Invert f'(a) and use that 1 plus a maximal-ideal element is a unit to force b = a (proof lines 42322-42325).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is about a local ring (R, m, kappa) and states that two roots a and b of a polynomial f in R[T] which are congruent modulo m and at which f' is not in m must be equal (statement lines 42310-42316). The proof expands f at a to write the vanishing difference of values as f'(a)(b-a) plus a multiple of (b-a)^2, inverts the derivative, and concludes because b-a lies in the maximal ideal so that 1 + f'(a)^{-1}c(b-a) is a unit (proof lines 42318-42325). The step that carries the content is the Taylor expansion, which the author states and leaves to the reader as routine; everything after it is the standard unit argument in a local ring. H2.
